title: What a missing key looks like
A browser asks the API directly
cmd: curl -s -i -X OPTIONS https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages -H 'Origin: http://localhost:8111' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: x-api-key,anthropic-version,content-type' | grep -iE '^(HTTP|Disallowed)'

title: Ask through our own endpoint
cmd: node server.js > server.log 2>&1 & SERVER=$!; for i in $(seq 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8111/ && break; sleep 0.5; done; curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8111/api/ask -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"question": "Name one use of an API key, in one sentence."}'; echo; kill $SERVER

title: Check the key is not in the page
cmd: node server.js > server.log 2>&1 & SERVER=$!; for i in $(seq 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8111/ && break; sleep 0.5; done; node check-leak.js; STATUS=$?; kill $SERVER; wait $SERVER 2>/dev/null; exit $STATUS

title: Show errors
cmd: node server.js > server.log 2>&1 & SERVER=$!; for i in $(seq 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8111/ && break; sleep 0.5; done; node test-errors.js; kill $SERVER; wait $SERVER 2>/dev/null; echo '--- same server with a model name that does not exist ---'; MODEL=no-such-model node server.js > server.log 2>&1 & SERVER=$!; for i in $(seq 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8111/ && break; sleep 0.5; done; curl -s -w '  (status %{http_code})\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8111/api/ask -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"question": "hello"}'; kill $SERVER; wait $SERVER 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; echo '--- server terminal ---'; cat server.log
